subject: Media Literacy
title: Diversifying Your News Sources
description: A micro-lesson that makes Diversifying Your News Sources usable.

hook.text: You read one newspaper for 20 years. You think you're well-informed. You're actually well-informed in one perspective.

buildup.text: Source diversity means regularly consuming news from outlets with different perspectives, owners, and formats.

discovery.text: Tools like AllSides pair left, center, and right coverage of the same story so you can compare framings.

twist.text: Diversifying is uncomfortable. Reading views you disagree with feels wrong — but that's the confirmation bias talking.

climax.text: The discomfort of reading opposing views is the feeling of your understanding expanding.

punchline.text: If your news never challenges you, it's not informing you. It's confirming you.

quiz.question: Why does diversifying news sources feel uncomfortable?
options: Confirmation bias makes opposing views feel wrong
